alternatives.argument: The carrier defines every Bernoulli polynomial by its own finite coefficient recursion, with denominators shown positive and nonzero. This is a complete local definition and is not dependent on the unavailable lecture URL.

The carrier proves the derivative and zero-mean identities from the recursion, derives endpoint equality by FTC, proves reflection by induction and affine substitution, and obtains odd-index zeros and boundedness. Scott §13.3 and the fetched NIST §24.2 provide independent context; the proof itself is complete in this item.

The carrier derives the finite formula by cellwise integration by parts, telescopes panel boundary terms, pairs odd/even Bernoulli recurrences, and bounds the retained periodic-polynomial remainder. Scott §13.3 and NIST §3.5(iii) independently cover the formula; the local proof supplies the complete argument.

The carrier applies the local finite formula one correction beyond the retained terms, absorbs that endpoint term into the remainder, and bounds the result uniformly in N. Its proof is complete and its only theorem premise is the locally proved Euler–Maclaurin item.

The carrier explicitly defines every finite nested trapezoid entry and the Richardson recurrence, including L=0. It makes no accuracy claim and does not rely on the unavailable source for correctness.

The carrier proves by induction on the table column that each recurrence cancels its matching h^(2j) term and propagates a uniform h^(2m+2) remainder. It uses the locally proved finite expansion; the source is contextual only.

The carrier states the nine exact rational weights and nodes. Their integrated-cardinal meaning and degree-nine exactness are established by the complete local rational-arithmetic lemma; Scott and NIST §3.5(iv) supply independent interpolatory-rule context.

The carrier expands the nine exact Lagrange products after an affine integer-grid substitution, integrates the coefficient lists exactly, and proves degree-eight reproduction plus the odd degree-nine case by symmetry. It is a complete local proof; Scott supplies the detailed interpolatory context.
